Support should treat this as a scanned-PDF OCR/citation problem and follow these steps:

- First determine whether the PDF is scanned/image-only; without OCR, scanned PDFs cannot be searched and citations cannot be generated [NL-006-S03].
- Check the upload metadata to see if the file is flagged as image-only, and confirm the customer's workspace has OCR enabled [NL-006-S03].
- Inspect the admin logs for the query to identify the retrieved source ID and section ID; then check the source document's status and the user's permissions, because citations are stripped for deprecated/stale sources or restricted-access documents [NL-006-S04].
- If the source is a scanned PDF, inspect the OCR logs to see whether page boundaries were missed during indexing [NL-006-S04] and verify that OCR completed without errors [NL-028-S03].
- Instruct the customer to inspect scan quality and, if possible, export the document from the source system as a digital, text-searchable PDF instead of scanning a printed sheet [NL-006-S03].
- If scanned files must be used, recommend the Advanced OCR Pipeline, which uses layout-aware vision models to reconstruct text [NL-006-S03].
- For OCR formatting issues, suggest converting tables to `.csv` or `.xlsx` and uploading them separately, or formatting tables with clear, dark grid lines [NL-006-S03].
- Direct workspace admins to the Admin Console/KnowledgeHub health dashboard to review indexing health and citation confidence; files flagged as scanned with low confidence should be re-uploaded with high-resolution OCR [NL-021-S05].
- If OCR completed but citations are still stale or point to the wrong location, re-index the folder to refresh vector mappings [NL-028-S03].
